subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and before/after hooks?
rationale: The requested mode would be a user-trusted security/product guarantee, and current code has multiple tool execution surfaces where a narrow process-global adapter flag could miss side effects.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but defer implementation until broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines shared preview semantics.

options.title: Keep scoped dry-runs only
options.body: Reject global dry-run if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue command-specific previews instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest verified history across the agent CLI Gateway routing and direct tool-invocation boundary.
